reading.body:
Russell Fry's AI record in this data is mostly money: 12 of 18 events are FEC contributions from Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and Google PACs, totaling $22,500 in positive receipts against $2,000 in refunded or reversed amounts.

The pattern is concentration. Amazon and Microsoft PACs account for $15,000 of the positive total, and the largest single contributions, $3,500 and $3,000, arrive in March and May 2026. Two Meta entries on 2025-03-26 show a $1,000 contribution and a matching $-1,000, and two later Meta entries show the same pairing, which reads as a refund or reclassification rather than new money.

The four recorded votes span April 2025 to June 2026, with three Yea and one Nay. The data does not include bill titles or subjects, so it cannot show whether any vote touched compute, data centers, or grid policy, and it draws no causal link between contributions and votes. What it establishes is proximity: AI-adjacent corporate PAC money and AI-bill votes sit in the same record for the same member.

What the data does not cover is the substance of the bills, the member's committee assignments, or any spending on AI policy beyond these PAC receipts. It also cannot distinguish a member who receives broad industry support from one whose positions align with a single sector, because no comparison set is given.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Russell Fry: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 18 events.
